Programme Aim The purpose of this training programme is to design, develop and deliver a training programme that build people’s understanding of self-harm and the role it plays in the life of a person who self-harms. The programme will build the knowledge and confidence of the learner to have a conversation if they are concerned that someone may be self-harming. The training programme should provide people who access it with a sense of hope and reassurance that people can build healthier coping mechanisms. Programme Objectives The training programme is intended to: Increase understanding of what self-harm is. Increase understanding of the relationship between self-harm and suicide. Build skills and confidence to engage with a person and speak openly about self-harm. Challenge the stigma surrounding self-harm Increase awareness of available supports and services Stage 1: An introduction to the subject of self-harm – communicating the ‘why’ functions of self-harm through lived experience experts. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi

references_experience.text: ct Title: Acquisition of 7T Ultra-High Field MRI System & Subsystems Amendment Number: 0001 Release Date: September 10, 2026 Item 1: Technical & Contractual Clarification Question: The solicitation states that FAR 52.212-3 and FAR 52.212-5 have been eliminated and replaced by individually incorporated provisions and clauses. Can the Government confirm that all clauses normally required under FAR 52.212-5 have been incorporated and identify where offerors may find the complete list of applicable FAR clauses? Government Response: Refer to Amendment 0001. The Government has modified Section I.1 to formally incorporate FAR 52.212-5 by reference, ensuring all mandatory commercial product and service statutes are legally preserved. The specific statutory sub-clauses applicable to this procurement (including equal opportunity, subcontracting enforcement, and supply chain cybersecurity) have been explicitly checked within that framework. The complete framework consists of the standalone provisions in Sections I and L, governed by the reinstated FAR 52.212-5 block. FAR 52.212-3 (Offeror Representations and Certifications) remains replaced by active, electronic vendor records maintained within SAM.gov under standard commercial streamlining procedures. Item 2: Technical & Contra

he Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) framework enacted via Executive Order 14275 (Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement) and governing agency class deviations, FAR 52.212-5 (Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders—Commercial Products and Commercial Services) has been completely deleted from the FAR system and is no longer used in any capacity. Accordingly, the solicitation is amended as follows: 1. Correction to Amendment 0001 Q&A Log (Item 1): Item 1 of the Q&A log released with Amendment 0001 is hereby rescinded in its entirety. The guidance stating that FAR 52.212- 5 was reinstated by reference or that a reinstated framework governs this procurement was issued in error. 2. Reaffirmation of FAR 52.212-5 Exclusion: FAR 52.212-5 remains completely excluded from this procurement. Offerors must not utilize the checkbox-driven master framework of FAR 52.212-5 for their compliance matrices, certifications, representations, or subcontract flow-down planning. 3. Controlling Clause Framework: The Government’s requirement relies strictly on direct, standalone clause insertion as set forth in the RFO Part 12 modernized rules. Only the specific standalone clauses explicitly written and listed in Section I of this solicitation apply.
